<a id="body"></a>

## Body

F227/#272 distinguishes observer retirement from owner intent. With no pending pij close, observed-dead leaves holdings open: views/routing exclude the dead seat, and revival restores its holdings without reassignment. Never turn a display/liveness filter into automatic holding release.

An already-authorized held close is different: observer retirement during its memory turn must not skip close_seat/end_holdings. Keep the original actor, current may_close recheck and descriptor CAS. Changed process OR pane and an owner-close already landed remain brakes; compact still skips every tombstone. POLICY is the explicit close; those checks only spare.

For role sends, filter the requested instance before live/dead classification. A dead reviewer/196 queues; it must never fall through to reviewer/197's live holder. New queued-reason diagnostics use only the addressed project's holdings and change no recipient or holding state. General shell-quoting guidance is already in the existing holding-data note.

Useful proof: changing live_seat to retain tombstoned rows fails all three dead-holder role-send regressions in directory_http.rs; restoring it passes. Changing the process/pane brake from OR to AND fails the action-brake unit test. Independently verified at 55cea7a841f93e8f1565ed368279ce6ff03fa5c9. Verdict commits: dac562c5 (round 1), 0f987c04 (final delta).
